subject: Post-demo recap: inference economics playbook & $/1M token targets
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@finlytics.ai>, Priya Mehta <priya.mehta@finlytics.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap: inference economics playbook & $/1M token targets

Hi Evan / Priya —

Thanks again for the demo earlier today — appreciate you walking us through the Finlytics ingestion and user flows. Per our ask during the call, I captured a short recap of the cost targets and some benchmark context to help procurement and finance evaluate options. See the short summary below and the attached two-pager (redwood_inference_pricing_summary.pdf) + our editable volume model (finlytics_volume_model.xlsx).

Quick factuals from the call you confirmed:
- Realistic steady-state traffic: 75M–120M tokens / month (peak bursts up to ~350M in market open hours)
- Workload profile: majority short-chat + some long-context summarization (avg request 240 tokens; policies for prefix caching)
- Data/sensitivity: PII redaction required; considering Private deployment for auditability in Q4

High-level $/1M token benchmarking (hosted entry pricing for reference):
- OpenAI (public list): approx $60–90 / 1M tokens depending on model family and ephemeral vs context handling
- Anthropic (public list): approx $55–80 / 1M tokens for their mid-tier chat models
- Other open-model hosts (varies by optimization): $40–120 / 1M tokens depending on quantization and batching profile

Redwood preliminary guidance (ballpark — can tighten with exact volume curve):
- Redwood Hosted (self-serve): $82 / 1M tokens list for the model family matching your quality bar (includes streaming + function-calling paths)
- Redwood Dedicated (reserved pool, single-tenant): $48–62 / 1M tokens depending on commit term and burst policy (we typically see customers in your volume range hit the low end after 12-month commit and autoscale tuning)
- Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem): price varies more; base platform + infra + support — we usually model to $60–75 / 1M tokens post infra amortization for mid-term contracts

Notes on what drives variance: batching strategy (more batching -> lower effective $/1M), quantization/accelerator choice, KV/prefix cache hit rate (saves tokens and reduces compute), and SLA/backfill windows. We've attached an excel model that shows how a 10% improvement in effective batching or a 20% KV hit rate shifts the unit economics.

A few concrete asks / next steps:
1) Can you confirm a more precise monthly token range (low / expected / high) and an expected contract term (12 vs 24 months)?
2) Who should we include from procurement/finance to surface the committed-cost numbers (name + email)?
3) Any hard $/1M target we should use when we size Dedicated vs Hosted options? You mentioned wanting to be competitive with X-host — if you can share a target $/1M that helps us model concession scenarios.

I'll schedule a short follow-up (15–20 min) to review the attached model if that works for you.

Thanks —
Monica Patel
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: redwood_inference_pricing_summary.pdf (2 pages), finlytics_volume_model.xlsx (Excel)
From: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@finlytics.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Mehta <priya.mehta@finlytics.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: inference economics playbook & $/1M token targets

Monica —

Thanks for the follow-up and the model. A couple quick clarifications from our side:
- The 75M–120M is our expected band; low ~50M in slower months, expected ~90M, high 180M in Q1 market events.
- Contract horizon: leaning toward 12 months initially with option to expand.
- Procurement contact: Priya Mehta (cc'd) will lead the finance/contract side.

Regarding price target — Finlytics has internal goals to get to roughly $45–50 / 1M tokens for the majority of production traffic after discounts and committed usage. We understand that's aggressive vs list, but that is the number we see as commercially viable for our margins.

Two asks: can Redwood map the Dedicated pricing bands to that target ($45–50) and show what committed volume/term would be required? Also want to confirm if there are any additional platform fees or per-seat admin charges when moving to Dedicated/Private.

Happy to hop on a quick call this week to walk through the excel.

—Evan
Evan Brooks
Head of Platform Engineering | Finlytics
ev an.brooks@finlytics.ai | +1 617-555-0102
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 11:12:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-demo recap: inference economics playbook & $/1M token targets

Internal note — summary of how we can approach Evan's $45–50 / 1M target (confidential internal calc):

Assumptions: monthly steady-state tokens = 90M, peak ratio = 2x, average tokens per request 240, model family = high-accuracy open model (cost heavier than trimmed small models).

Paths to hit $45–50 / 1M:
1) Dedicated reserved + 12–18 month commit with aggressive autoscale capping -> we can model to $50 / 1M at ~90–120M tokens/mo if they commit to a 12-month reservation with 75% utilization on dedicated pool. This requires a 15–20% discount on base dedicated list and close collaboration on batching + KV caching (we help with config).
2) Private (VPC) with customer-managed infra -> blended economics depend on infra amortization; to get to $45 we'd be pushing more operational cost to Finlytics (they absorb infra), but platform fee would be reduced.
3) Hybrid: Redwood Dedicated for peak-critical routes and Hosted for lower-value batch jobs -> effective blended $/1M can be $46–55 depending on traffic split.

Other levers: model quantization (8-bit or 4-bit) and early-token offload for summarization workloads. Engineering effort: ~2–3 sprints for a joint optimization plan (tuning batching, prefix cache policies, and a small inference wrapper).

Recommended next steps (internal):
- Prepare a dedicated offer sheet with three bands: Silver (12m commit), Gold (12m higher commit + caching plan), Platinum (24m + operational SLA + onboarding support).
- Build two scenarios in the attached finlytics_volume_model.xlsx: conservative (50–75M), expected (90–120M). Pin the margin sensitivity.

I can assemble the offer draft — Monica, if you want I can include suggested discount tiers and corresponding commit thresholds by EOD tomorrow.

—Jonas
Director, Solutions Architecture | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: inference economics playbook & $/1M token targets

Evan / Priya —

Appreciate the clarity on the $45–50 target. We've run the initial scenarios and have a concrete next step proposal:

Offer preview (high level):
- 12-month Dedicated commitment (Gold): commit 90M tokens/month -> list blended starting at $58 / 1M tokens with a performance & batching optimization plan that we guarantee to implement within first 60 days. With staged discounts tied to usage/uptake, we can move to $49 / 1M if 90M sustained for 6 months.
- 24-month (Platinum): commit 120M tokens/month -> starting $52 / 1M with pathway to $45 / 1M after 3 months of optimizations and a 24-month ARR commitment.
- Hosted fallback: ongoing Hosted access as overflow at $82 / 1M list (used only for burst overflow above Dedicated capacity).

Platform fees: no separate per-seat admin fees for Dedicated. Private/VPC incurs an additional platform management fee (we can scope if you want that path). All discounts and SLAs will be captured in the formal MSA addendum.

Next steps I propose:
1) I'll send a formal offer sheet + term summary (PDF) and a short 20-min call to align procurement.
2) Priya — can you share the procurement contact and the preferred cadence for legal review? Also, confirm if Finlytics requires SOC2 Type II evidence (we can provide the package).
3) If you want to push to the Platinum pathway, let me know and Jonas will draft the detailed optimization milestones and success criteria.

I'll attach the offer-preview and a DocuSign link for an NDA + LOI placeholder once we align.

Best,
Monica Patel
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
